clue.text: Money may be obtained from many a debtor

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, a crossword stand-in for a large number
an ower is someone who owes, i.e. a debtor

explanation.surface: A remark that cash can be squeezed out of plenty of people in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many' is the crossword convention for D, the Roman 500.
explanation.definitionFit: A widow's portion of her late husband's estate is property or income, hence money.

clue.text: Underworld boss put on edge over a good man's lying

parts.note: Dis is the Roman ruler of the underworld
to hone is to sharpen, giving a blade its edge
ST, saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A gang boss sharpening a knife above a decent man who is telling fibs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just stacks the pieces in order; 'Underworld boss' is the god Dis, not a gangster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying is being untruthful, the core sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Don't claim a view isn't right

indicators.note: something that isn't right is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice not to assert that someone's opinion is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't right' rearranges the letters of A VIEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo or give up a right is to decline to claim it.

clue.text: Practised play

parts.note: a stage piece that has been gone over in advance is described by the adjective, and the same word means practised

explanation.definitionFit: A drama run through beforehand by the cast is one they have practised, the adjective's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Sort of plants made up in bales perhaps

indicators.note: letters made into something new are reworked, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of up in bales are the fodder; perhaps adds no letters and only hedges that this is one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: A farmer's crop baled up as some kind of plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges UP IN BALES, with 'perhaps' only a hedge; the plants grow on slopes below the treeline.
explanation.definitionFit: Subalpine flora grow on mountain slopes just below the treeline, a botanical category of vegetation.

clue.text: A quarter continue to list this cheese

indicators.note: to here means one piece is added to the end of another

parts.note: S, south, is one quarter of the compass
a ship that lists leans over, or tilts
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: Instructions to keep adding a fraction to a list of cheeses.
explanation.walkthrough: Stilton is a strong blue-veined English cheese; the 'quarter' is a compass point, not a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a blue-veined English cheese, an example of the class.

clue.text: Flower as a result of insecticide use?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a bloom is the outcome of spraying chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for what spraying insects causes; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The plant is a blue-flowered herb of the borage family, while a split reading gives the death of pests from spraying.

clue.text: The old doctor's a sucker!

explanation.surface: Mocking a physician of former times as a parasite.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic word for a physician is also the bloodsucking worm doctors once applied.
explanation.definitionFit: In old English usage a physician was called by this word, and the same word is the bloodsucking worm.

clue.text: Popular instrument — a single note shows nothing can touch it

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a viola is a stringed instrument
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A favourite instrument playing one note that proves it beyond reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inviolate is unharmed and untouchable, safe from any interference.

clue.text: A resort of high-fliers

parts.note: reads like a holiday spot for the jet set, but means the lofty nest of eagles and other birds of prey

explanation.definitionFit: An eagle's nest built on a crag is a haunt of birds that fly very high.

clue.text: Scoring to produce notes without illumination

indicators.note: without here means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
light is illumination

explanation.surface: Disdainfully singing in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, the older sense, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Slighting someone means treating them with disdain, the same as scorning them.

clue.text: Young swimmer constantly seen around small lake

indicators.note: around means one piece is wrapped about the other

parts.note: ever means always or constantly
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A youngster always to be found swimming round a little lake.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a fish that swims upriver.

clue.text: Gained nothing by a musical performance

parts.note: gaining nothing means scoring zero, the letter O
per means by, as in per post

explanation.surface: Someone got nothing out of attending a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Opera is a staged drama set to music and sung, a form of musical show.

clue.text: Being very nice over the MO's error

indicators.note: over places this piece ahead of the next

parts.note: too means very, as in not too bad

indicators.note: an error is a mistake, so these letters come out wrong and need rearranging

explanation.surface: A doctor's blunder being made to seem pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'error' rearranges THE MOS into THSOME; MO is a medical officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome food is tasty, and the word extends to anything appealing or attractive.

clue.text: Writer taking issue after a military body's retreat

indicators.note: after places the son piece at the end
to retreat is to go back, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps
issue means offspring, such as a son

explanation.surface: An author arguing with an army unit as it withdraws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' reads REME backwards to give EMER; REME is a British Army engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist and poet, an example of an author.

clue.text: Greek dramatist prepared for rough ride is up without direction

indicators.note: without here means outside, putting this letter on the edge of the rest

parts.note: E, east, is a compass direction

indicators.note: a rough version is disordered, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Greek playwright getting ready for a bumpy, aimless journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' rearranges RIDE IS UP into URIPIDES, with E outside it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: He was one of the three great Athenian tragedians, author of Medea.

clue.text: They are no singers of low songs!

definitions.text: They are no singers of low songs!

parts.words: They are no singers of low songs!
parts.note: seems to praise refined performers, but means high voices who never sing the low parts

explanation.definitionFit: Italian plural for the highest female voices, who cannot sing bass lines.

clue.text: She'll pay for catty utterance about Charles English!

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the others

parts.note: a purr is the sound a cat makes

explanation.surface: A woman paying for a spiteful remark about an Englishman named Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catty' means cat-like, not spiteful here.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyer is the person who pays for goods.

clue.text: Finding rent etc is possibly making one cross

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be put another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Discovering that the rent and extras are probably enough to annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges RENT ETC IS; 'cross' is the verb, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To intersect is to cut across, which is what lines do when they meet.

clue.text: One involved in deals will get streams of abuse

parts.note: trades are deals
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man caught up in shady dealings gets shouted at.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirades are long angry speeches, torrents of insult.

clue.text: An immigrant arranging 27?

explanation.surface: A newcomer sorting out a release.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 is DISCHARGE: one who settles a bill discharges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonist arriving to live in a new land is one sense; someone who pays off a debt is the other.

clue.text: Turned colour and left the river

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour
went means left, departed

explanation.surface: Someone blushed and walked off from the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses RED; the Derwent is one of several English rivers of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derwent flows through Derbyshire and the Lake District, an example of a waterway.

clue.text: Get mad with some trader, angered beyond tolerance

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is found within these words

explanation.surface: A dealer, angered past endurance, flies into a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'trader, angered', in tradeR ANGEred.
explanation.definitionFit: To derange is to drive insane, to make someone lose their reason.

clue.text: Drink with stout defender

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer like stout

explanation.surface: A loyal fan having a pint of stout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stout' looks like an adjective for the defender, but is the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter backs and upholds a cause, like a champion or advocate.

clue.text: Repaired for only five hundred!

parts.note: sole means only
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A bargain mend costing just five hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoes that have been resoled are mended by fitting new bottoms.

clue.text: Black magic

parts.note: witchcraft of the kind practised in the Caribbean

explanation.definitionFit: A form of sorcery from the West Indies, of African origin.

clue.text: He really doesn't like causing heart-break

indicators.note: break means smash, so the letters are scattered and put together anew

explanation.surface: A man who dislikes breaking hearts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' rearranges HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who loathes something feels strong dislike, a person full of enmity.

clue.text: Object when spare key is demanded

parts.note: spare means lean or thin
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: An item asked for when a spare key is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' means lean, not extra; the key is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is any item or article, the most general noun for an entity.

clue.text: The home of a man of science

explanation.surface: Referring to the house where a scientist lived.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist and radio pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small house such as a gatekeeper's is one sense; the physicist Sir Oliver of that surname is the other.

clue.text: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip

definitions.text: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip

parts.words: A lack of good grounding was responsible for this slip
parts.note: sounds like an error caused by poor education, but means earth giving way down a slope

explanation.definitionFit: When unstable soil fails, a hillside collapses in a mass movement of earth.

clue.text: Deputy-head is to tax pay

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word

parts.note: to charge is to levy a tax or fee

explanation.surface: An instruction that the assistant chief should levy wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deputy-head' looks like a school post, but 'head' just takes the first letter of 'Deputy'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discharge a debt is to settle it, i.e. to pay it off.

clue.text: Blue or quite proper?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a Conservative is truly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of the British Conservative party, the political right.
explanation.definitionFit: Conservatives are politically on the right wing, and correct or fitting conduct is the other sense.
